stem: A Massachusetts community pharmacy receives a medication after prescription processing was performed outside its premises at another pharmacy licensed by the Massachusetts Board. No separate Massachusetts pharmacist re-verifies that offsite processing at the receiving pharmacy. The pharmacist on duty inspects the finished medication before dispensing. Which assessment is most accurate?

choices.text: Dispensing is prohibited because every offsite process must be separately re-verified at the receiving pharmacy.
The Board-licensed offsite pharmacy satisfies an alternative condition for dispensing, without treating the final inspection as verification of the process.
The final inspection alone satisfies the rule, whether or not the offsite pharmacy is licensed by the Board.
The medication may be dispensed only if the offsite pharmacy also shares ownership with the receiving pharmacy.
The medication may be dispensed because any pharmacy license issued by any jurisdiction satisfies the offsite-site condition.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.04(11) supplies two alternative conditions for medication processed outside the dispensing pharmacy's licensed premises: the process was verified by a Massachusetts-licensed pharmacist, or the process was performed in a pharmacy licensed by the Massachusetts Board. The facts satisfy the second condition. The receiving pharmacist's inspection may be prudent, but it is not what converts an otherwise noncompliant offsite process into a compliant one.

choice_analysis.A: Separate Massachusetts-pharmacist verification is one alternative, not an additional requirement after Board-licensed-site processing.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: processing at a pharmacy licensed by the Board independently satisfies the regulation's site-based alternative.
choice_analysis.C: Inspection of the product is not verification of how the offsite process was performed.
choice_analysis.D: Common ownership is not stated as a condition of either alternative.
choice_analysis.E: The site-based alternative requires a pharmacy licensed by the Massachusetts Board, not merely a license from another jurisdiction.

related_facts: A Massachusetts-licensed pharmacist may satisfy the separate verification alternative even when the site-based alternative is unavailable
explanation.mpje_trap: The final inspection is the most visible act in the workflow, but the regulation focuses on who verified the process or where the process occurred.

reasoning_steps: Identify that processing occurred outside the dispensing pharmacy's premises
Determine whether either regulatory alternative was satisfied
Distinguish Board licensure of the processing site from pharmacist verification
Avoid treating a finished-product inspection as retrospective process verification
